entities.summary: Papa Stour is one of the Shetland Islands in Scotland, with a population of fifteen people, some of whom immigrated after an appeal for residents in the 1970s. Located to the west of mainland Shetland and with an area of 828 hectares, Papa Stour is the ninth largest island in Shetland. Erosion of the soft volcanic rocks by the sea has created an extraordinary variety of caves, stacks, arches, blowholes, and cliffs. The island and its surrounding seas harbour diverse populations of wildlife. The west side of the island is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and the seas around the island are a Special Area of Conservation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Papa Stour's unique geological features and diverse wildlife populations contribute to its significance as a regional conservation site, supporting biodiversity in Northern Europe. The island's Site of Special Scientific Interest designation highlights the importance of preserving this unique ecosystem.
